source.title: Theoretical Insights Into the Optimization Landscape of Over-Parameterized Shallow Neural Networks
source.authors: M. Soltanolkotabi; Adel Javanmard; J. Lee

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including the main results, numerical experiments, proofs, and references.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes and numerically tests gradient-based optimization of shallow networks on synthetic data, including random labels; these results bear conceptually on training error, but do not reproduce the benchmark experiments or architectures in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's numerical experiments and theorems on training loss bear on V1 and V2. It does not test the listed benchmark architectures, depth, initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability phenomena, or batch normalization. References to results from other work, including [55], are cited prior findings and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports squared-loss regression and optimization-landscape results for shallow fully connected networks with softplus or quadratic activations. These do not measure V1's convolutional-network classification error or V2's ReLU teacher-student width comparison. Its own results do not test V3–V6 either. References to the original findings motivate the work rather than supply a tested outcome.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: overparameterization yields favorable quadratic-network landscapes, and smooth-activation gradient descent has a local linear-convergence guarantee. Experiments suggest improved global optimization with parameter count, including random targets. The claimed zero-loss interpretation of the random-target softplus experiment requires clarification because its stated positive-output architecture cannot fit negative targets.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies one-hidden-layer synthetic networks and squared training loss, with theoretical landscape results and small numerical experiments; it does not apply the benchmark recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with width/input dimension in the planted-data experiments; the random-label experiments report global minima when kd > 1.5n.

fits_no_version.finding: The random-target experiments report improved regression optimization with width and global minima for kd>1.5n; the softplus setup and width range contain unresolved inconsistencies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficient overparameterization can improve gradient-descent fitting of random real-valued targets in shallow regression networks, subject to representational constraints.

fits_no_version.finding: Under specified width, output-weight signs, rank, and data conditions, quadratic networks have no spurious local minima, strict saddles, and zero global loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Certain overparameterized shallow quadratic regression networks have favorable optimization landscapes.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient descent converges linearly in squared loss from sufficiently close planted initialization under the theorem's assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shallow planted regression networks with suitable smooth activations admit local linear convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing width or input dimension increases the empirical frequency of all initialization trials reaching global minima in planted softplus and quadratic regression experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing the parameter-to-sample ratio improves empirical optimization success in these shallow planted regression settings.

record.problems: Synthetic, shallow one-hidden-layer settings rather than CIFAR benchmarks; the general-activation convergence result requires close initialization; experiment counts are limited to 10 generated planted models and 10 initialization trials per model; Figure 3 prose and caption specify inconsistent settings; Figure 4 gives no individual RMSE values in text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying outcomes identified beyond rows R1–R9. The cited empirical results from Zhang et al. [55] and other cited studies are prior work, not this study's own results.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional classification on CIFAR-10/100, SGD or Adam from random initialization, random or corrupted class labels, and smaller-model or regularization comparisons.
ReLU teacher-student optimization, increasing matched teacher/student widths, and adding one or two student neurons relative to the teacher.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated deep-network alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, initialization comparisons, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to initial stability, catapult recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on accuracy gains and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions; this does not negate the study's regression results. Conditions required by a theorem are not evidence that a listed version fails outside those conditions.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR benchmarks, convolutional networks, Adam, corrupted labels, early stopping, or smaller-model substantial-error comparison. Experiments use one-hidden-layer networks and synthetic Gaussian inputs and labels.
The paper does not study two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks or compare student width with teacher width.
No depth sweep, identity shortcuts, ImageNet or CIFAR-10, or shortcut-free deep tanh/residual models.
No comparison of activation-matched versus other initializations, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, or very deep plain convolutional networks.
No learning-rate sweep around a stability limit, catapult phase, sharpness tracking, or divergence comparisons.
No batch normalization comparison, training-speed or learning-rate-tolerance measure, or Fixup comparison.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer network with softplus activation
rows.size_stated: d = 10, n = 100; k varies from 3 to 13
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent fit softplus network to independently random Gaussian inputs and labels; RMSE plotted against iterations.

conditions.value: k varies; text says kd > 1.5n yields a global minimizer

rows.value: Figure 4a: figure only; text says gradient descent finds a global minimizer when kd > 1.5n.
rows.note: The text describes zero RMSE as the width increases, but the plot's individual curve values are not transcribed in text.
rows.check: Regression objective values do not measure V1's classification error. Figure 4a lists k=8–13, not 3–13; with d=10 and n=100, none satisfies kd>1.5n. The stated fixed positive output weights also make softplus outputs positive, preventing exact fitting of negative Gaussian targets. The text's zero-loss interpretation therefore needs clarification.

rows.subject: quadratic-activation shallow network with fixed hidden-output weights
rows.operation_detail: Theorem establishes global optimality and zero residual for gradient descent on input-to-hidden weights, under its stated conditions.

conditions.value: arbitrary input/label pairs; for zero-optimum conclusion, almost every input data set
at least d positive and at least d negative entries

rows.value: Global optimum is zero; proof concludes r = 0.
rows.note: This is a theorem about a restricted quadratic shallow network and a chosen output-layer sign pattern, not a CIFAR experiment.
rows.check: This is a conditional quadratic-network landscape and zero-optimum theorem, not a measured classification-training outcome. The theorem itself does not give an explicit gradient-descent convergence rate; the accompanying discussion draws the random-initialization convergence implication.

rows.subject: planted two-layer network with quadratic activation
rows.operation_detail: Theorem establishes that global optima have zero training loss under a planted model and stated sign conditions.

conditions.value: planted model; almost every input data set
generated by planted two-layer network; nonzero entries of v* share a sign
nonzero entries share the sign of v* and at least d are nonzero

rows.note: The result is conditional on a planted model and does not establish that random initialization reaches this optimum empirically.
rows.check: The planted quadratic-network theorem establishes landscape properties and zero global loss, not V1's classification result or V2's ReLU width comparison. Add the required full-column-rank condition on W*.

rows.subject: planted two-layer network with general differentiable activation
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent converges linearly in loss from initial weights required to be sufficiently close to the planted weights.

conditions.value: differentiable, bounded first and second derivatives, satisfying Assumption 2.3(a) or Remark 2.6(b)
W0 and v0 obey closeness bounds (2.4)–(2.5)

rows.note: The theorem explicitly requires initialization close to the planted solution, so it does not test random initialization.
rows.check: Local squared-loss convergence from an initialization close to planted weights does not test random-initialization classification training, activation-matched signal propagation, or trainable depth. The sample-size bound uses sigma_min(W*)^4/sigma_max(W*)^8, rather than the fourth power of their ratio.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer network with softplus activation
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent from random initialization tested across widths; reported as finding global minima for all trials at sufficiently large widths.

conditions.value: planted Gaussian model; xi ∼ N(0, Id), yi = ⟨v*, φ(W*xi)⟩
v0 i.i.d. Rademacher ±1; W0 i.i.d. N(0,1)/√d

rows.measure: Whether gradient descent finds a global minimizer across random initializations
rows.value: For k ≥ 13 every single local minimizer found by gradient descent is a global minimizer.
rows.uncertainty: 10 experiments per (n,k,d); 10 random-initialization trials per W*
rows.note: The paper says it declares no spurious local minima when every initialization trial reaches a global minimum.
rows.check: The measured outcome is successful regression optimization across initialization trials. Teacher and student widths vary together; there is no comparison giving the student extra neurons relative to a fixed teacher, and the activation is softplus. Successful trials also do not prove absence of all spurious minima.

rows.measure: Whether gradient descent finds a global minimizer across random initializations
rows.value: For d ≥ 12, gradient descent always finds a global minimizer.
rows.uncertainty: 10 experiments per (n,k,d); 10 random-initialization trials per W*
rows.note: The paper says it declares no spurious local minima when every initialization trial reaches a global minimum.
rows.check: This varies input dimension and measures regression optimization success, rather than classification error or the ReLU teacher-student width intervention. The probability concerns all ten initializations succeeding for each generated teacher, not a proof of landscape-wide absence of spurious minima.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic shallow-network settings with random labels at sufficiently large width and the stated quadratic theorem conditions
reader_labels.reason: The text reports global-minimum/zero-loss outcomes for random-label synthetic data and proves zero loss for a restricted quadratic shallow network (R1–R4). These results support the training-error claim only in the tested shallow synthetic settings.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Random-initialization planted-data width sweeps and local convergence from a close planted initialization
reader_labels.reason: The experiments report global minima only at sufficiently large tested widths, and the general-activation theorem requires initialization close to the planted weights (R5–R7).
